messages:
katie: Heads-up — FinX POC asking for EU-only inference with APAC failover and a strict 'no-US-egress' expectation. They also want a per-region subprocessor list and a delta on pricing if we pin a tenant to eu-west. Can someone help today? Their desired kickoff: next week (start of May).

matt: I can run numbers. Quick clarifying q: do they want BYOK (customer-managed keys) in eu-west or CP-managed keys for the POC?

katie: BYOK preferred — they mentioned Azure Key Vault (westeurope). Also asked for a p95 latency SLA for EU during POC: target 99.9% p95. Typical load for POC: ~1k reqs/min, avg payload ~150 tokens.

lee: For a p95 target at that QPS, we should use Dedicated capacity pinned to eu-west. Hosted may be unpredictable due to noisy neighbors. With Dedicated and our optimized kernels we can realistically get p95 ~100-120ms for small/medium models.

anya: Security note: I'll pull the latest subprocessor attestation. High level: for hosted we currently list AWS (eu-west-1, eu-west-2), GCP (europe-west2), Azure (westeurope) — for Dedicated it's customer-chosen infra. I'll attach the PDF.

matt: Pricing delta: tenant pin + reserved capacity + BYOK integration is roughly +40% over baseline hosted for the stated volume. I'll model a 3-month POC SOW and post a table.

sre-oncall: Ops caveat: APAC failover is doable but needs explicit routing rules. We replicate metadata (cache/KV pointers) cross-region; user data path can be routed to APAC. To meet 'no-US-egress' we must ensure egress hops avoid us regions — that depends on carrier/backbone. Legal will want careful wording.

katie: Any technical blockers on Azure Key Vault BYOK integration? Customer wants a diagram for legal.

anya: Minor blocker: in hosted mode we support key wrapping with Azure KV but require a service principal + managed identity from the customer. I'll document the exact steps they need to provision. Also need to confirm FR-proc for key escrow policies.

matt: I'll draft a POC SOW today: environment matrix, pinned region, throughput targets, SLA, BYOK steps, fallback policy, and cost table. ETA EOD.

ops-bot: playbook created: /playbooks/poc-finX/ — tasks assigned to @lee @matt @anya. Check-ins scheduled: daily stand 09:30 UTC starting next Monday.

lee: One more ops item: fallback behavior if eu capacity constrained — we can failover to an EU-quantized model variant (same region) to preserve residency and reduce memory pressure. We should document fallback order and approval gate for legal.

katie: Miguel in Legal asked for an explicit statement 'no-US-egress'. Can we provide that to them?

anya: We can commit to 'no intentional US egress under normal operations' but cannot guarantee absolute zero transient hops on global backbones. Suggest legal text: "No-US-egress under normal operations; in disaster recovery scenarios minimal transient routes may occur as documented in the network appendix." I'll upload suggested wording to the playbook.

matt: Posted draft cost table + a sample 3-month SOW to the playbook. Pricing assumptions included: model class = 'medium', avg tokens = 150, reqs/min = 1000, pinned dedicated pool with 24/7 reserved capacity.

katie: Thanks all. Plan: 1) confirm BYOK steps with customer, 2) share subproc attestation + legal wording, 3) send SOW and price delta, 4) ops runbook for failover and fallback. Ping me ASAP if any blocker — FinX wants to kick off next week. :thumbsup:
